# dsh-git-graph-sidebar
English | 中文
A Git plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): a branch chip in the composer, a **Repository graph** tab i
nside dsh-better-sidebar, and — opt-in — the same graph as a page in the conversation's main area. I
t lists the Git repositories found up to three levels below the workspace, draws the selected reposi
tory's commit graph as an SVG lane canvas, and turns that repository's commit conventions into somet
hing both you and the model actually follow.
## Why this one
Plenty of plugins draw a commit graph. This one is built around the part that decides whether a comm
it message comes out right, and the three guarantees below are not on offer elsewhere:
1. **The rules reach the model, not just the panel.** The convention document is registered as a `sy
stemPrompt` section, so every model step is told what this repository wants before it writes anythin
g, instead of learning it from a rejection. `strict: true` goes further: the block tells the assista

nt to rewrite an offending message before committing.
2. **The rules are read back, prose included.*
* Machine-checkable rules (type prefixes, subject length, case, trailing period, mood, subject langu
age) are parsed out of the document — and out of an `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursorrules` or `CON
TRIBUTING.md` sitting beside it — so a repository that never wrote a `GIT_CONVENTIONS.md` is still u
nderstood. A backward-compatible `ai: required | optional | forbidden` field then checks the trailer

s in commit **bodies**, which is where attribution actually lives.
3. **Two documents that disagree
never get silently outvoted.** Dropping a plugin into a running project is the usual way a second co
nvention document appears. The tab compares the workspace document, the repository document and a pa
rent repository's document field by field and rule by rule, the injected block asks the agent to che
ck with you before picking a side, and the agent merges them into `<workspace>/.dsh/GIT_CONVENTIONS.

md` with timestamped backups and pointer files the plugin then follows.
4. **Three entry points, one
body.** The same tab renders in the better-sidebar tab, and — behind a switch, closable at any time
— as a page beside *对话* / *轨迹* in the conversation area, so the graph can be widened without leavin
g the sidebar as the primary entry.
Everything runs locally against the loopback endpoint the host already provides: no network calls, n
o telemetry, and every Git command is a read except the switches you press yourself.
## What it does
### Repository graph tab (better-sidebar)
The tab works from the session's working directory and treats that directory as a container: Git rep
ositories up to three levels below it are reachable without registering each repository as a separat
three levels below it are reachable without registering each repository as a separate DSH workspace.
- **Multi-repository discovery** — the workspace root itself, plus repositories nested up to 3 level
s below it. Each entry carries its current branch, short head, dirty-file count and conflict count.
- **A scan that costs what it should** — one `git for-each-ref` per repository returns the branch ti
me, the upstream and the ahead/behind distance in one call; while the refs have not moved the whole
answer comes from the last scan, and only the status probe (dirty files, conflicts) is repeated. A w

orkspace full of repositories no longer gets slower with every extra one.
- **Repository tree** — th
e root, the intermediate directories and each repository, so the level relationship between them is

visible rather than implied by a path.
- **Linked checkouts, read-only** — a repository row expands
to its linked worktrees (`git worktree list`), each with its branch and HEAD. Picking one switches t
he status strip to that checkout's branch, HEAD and dirty state and marks its HEAD row on the graph
— one graph, not one per checkout: linked worktrees share refs and objects, so the commit list is th
e same everywhere. From there the checkout opens in a new session, opens as a workspace, or its path
is copied; a checkout that is not registered as a workspace says so instead of failing silently, an
d a directory that was removed still shows in the list. The tab never creates, removes or switches a

worktree — that stays in the chip's dialog.
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements
| Item | Value |
idebar` | needed **for the tab only** — without it the plugin still loads and the chip keeps working
ebar` | needed **for the tab only** — without it the plugin still loads and the chip keeps working |
## Known limitations
- **The tab never changes an existing repository's Git state.** It writes the conventions document,
and it can run `git init` for a directory that is not a repository yet — nothing else. No commits, n
o branch switching, no worktree creation or removal: those stay in the chip's dialog. Linked checkou
ts are listed read-only, and a jump only opens a session or a workspace — it never creates a worktre

e.
- **Linked checkouts outside every registered workspace are listed but not readable.** The four `
/git/worktree/*` routes gate the *repository* the checkout belongs to, so a checkout that is not reg
istered as a workspace itself still gets its branch, HEAD and dirty state; the jump then registers i

t on request.
- **Do not install this alongside `@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-git-graph`.** Both halves
own the `/git` route prefix, and two registrations of the same prefix conflict. Install one or the o

ther.
- **Repositories deeper than 3 levels are not listed**, and a repository inside a skipped dire

ctory name (`node_modules`, `dist`, …) is not listed either, by design.
- **The host half is a build
output.** `lib/index.js` is edited directly (the added parts sit in marked `//#region` blocks); `li
b/client.js` is generated by splicing `src/client/graph/SidebarTab.js` into it. See DEVELOPMENT.md.
